subject: Reserved capacity — failover, preemption & on-call operational plan
messages:

Cc: contracts@peregrine.ai

Subject: Dedicated pool scaling + preempt policy questions

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re narrowing down the committed slab for Q1 and have a few operational questions before we sign:

- We expect a daily 2–3 hour peak (ML training / heavy inference) where our load can jump 4x; we’d like guidance on graceful overflow into ephemeral capacity vs preemption.
- What are Redwood’s preemption signals and typical notification window for Reserved pools?
- We need an on-call escalation and runbook for when burst fallback causes higher latency to our endpoints (SLA impacts).

I attached a quick spreadsheet with our projected hourly profiles. Can we get an ops-level plan (on-call rotations, failover choreography, crediting model during overflow)?

Simon
CTO, Peregrine AI

Attachment: Peregrine_Surge_Reqs_Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-13T10:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool scaling + preempt policy questions

Hi Simon —

Appreciate the spreadsheet; useful visibility. High-level answers below and I’ve sketched an ops playbook we can formalize in the SOW:

1) Overflow behavior:
   - Primary: route to Peregrine’s reserved slab until headroom exhausted.
   - Secondary: automatically route compatible requests to Redwood ephemerals (best-effort) under the same route with a configurable fallback policy.

2) Preemption signals / window:
   - Preemption is signal-driven at the process level with a 45–120s soft-notify window for active sessions and a hard-evict at "t0+180s" when resources need immediate reclamation.
   - We expose a callback webhook (POST /v1/ops/preempt_notify) and a token-level header you can use to surface degraded routing to downstream services.

3) Crediting & SLA:
   - For overflow that routes to Redwood ephemerals, we propose a crediting model: 50% of the per-token delta cost beyond reserved baseline as a post-billing credit (applies to the overflow window only).

4) On-call & runbook: initial proposal below.

Next steps: I’ll circulate a short runbook draft and a proposed on-call rotation for Redwood and Peregrine to approve. If that sounds good I’ll also add the DocuSign SLA amendment link for signature.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-14T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool scaling + preempt policy questions — Ops details

Team —

I put together a more operational set of items for the runbook (copied below). This is targeted at the SRE oncall and the customer’s platform engineers. Suggest we include as an appendix to the SOW and enforce during the 90-day onboarding period.

Operational summary (actionable):
- Surge windows: classify windows as micro-burst (<10m), sustained surge (10m–4h), and spike (4h+). For Peregrine we expect sustained surge daily.
- Headroom thresholds: soft throttle at 70% reserved utilization; start route-to-ephemeral at 80%; hard-preempt at 95% if no capacity reclaimed.
- Preemption notification: webhook at t-120s (soft), t-45s (escalation), t-0s (eviction). Webhook payload includes job-id, user-token, active-kv-size, and suggested fallback route.
- On-call rotations: Redwood provides L1 during business hours (M–F 08:00–18:00 PST) and L2 escalation 24/7 with a 30-min response SLA. Peregrine to provide a 24/7 contact list that can accept paging via PagerDuty.
- Credit calculation: credits apply only to requests routed to ephemeral during the surge window. Crediting formula: credit = max(0, (ephemeral_unit_cost - reserved_effective_cost) * 0.5 * ephemeral_units_consumed). We’ll add a worked example in the SOW.
- Telemetry: enable per-route token traces, per-request latency buckets, and an alert when ephemeral routing >10% for a rolling 1h window.

Ops doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Peregrine+Reserved+Failover+Runbook

I’ll draft the DocuSign amendment and loop in Legal if Peregrine is comfortable with the crediting approach. Thoughts?

—Aditya
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool scaling + preempt policy questions — DocuSign and numbers

Simon —

Thanks — we made the adjustments and attached the DocuSign. Quick answers inline and the credit worked example below.

- Soft-notify shortened to t-60s (we can log t-120s internally for prewarming metrics but will send customer-facing soft-notify at t-60s).
- Credit worked example (3h sustained surge, 120k ephemeral units):
   - Assumptions: reserved_effective_cost = $0.0015/unit; ephemeral_unit_cost = $0.0040/unit.
   - Delta per unit = $0.0040 - $0.0015 = $0.0025
   - Credit = 0.5 * delta * units = 0.5 * $0.0025 * 120,000 = $150

- L2 response SLA: Redwood confirms 30-min acknowledgement for L2 pages during the 90-day onboarding; we will include SLA clause in the amendment.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/ri/DEAL-2026-PEREG-0042

Next: Jasmine — please schedule a 30-minute kickoff with Peregrine infra + our SRE and Legal to finalize the SOW language and sign.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
